data.narrative:
Mariana Minerals is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Turner Caldwell that has raised $95M+ to date. The sector universe includes 9 peers across Climate & Energy, comprising 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Only one valuation method was applicable to this analysis. The Stage-Progression approach, anchored to the $95M total raised as a proxy for current valuation, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding $190M. A Peer-Median approach was not feasible: while 9 same-sector comparables exist, none met minimum thresholds (≥3 datapoints) when filtered by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier, rendering a narrow peer benchmark unreliable. A broad-sector median would introduce unacceptable distortion given the heterogeneity of climate technology maturity levels.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, centered at $190M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up multiplier for this cohort—climate tech Series A rounds exhibit variable investor appetites—and the lack of tight peer anchors to cross-validate the progression assumption. Given the limited methodological triangulation, this estimate should be treated as preliminary pending additional comparable transaction data or revenue/path-to-profitability detail.
